content.text:
What changed:

- **`MaxHeapCondition`** — a `@FunctionalInterface` with `boolean shouldPromote(int candidate, int current)`. The name is deliberately value-neutral so the same signature works for both orderings. Static factories `maxOrder()` (`>`) and `minOrder()` (`<`) provide the two standard heap variants as lambdas.

- **`HeapifyStrategy.of(int[] arr, MaxHeapCondition condition)`** — the generic factory that now drives the lambda. The raw `arr[l] > arr[dominant]` comparison is replaced by `condition.shouldPromote(arr[l], arr[dominant])`, removing all heap-type knowledge from the algorithm body.

- **`HeapifyStrategy.maxHeapify`** — kept as a named convenience that delegates to `of(arr, MaxHeapCondition.maxOrder())`, so existing call sites are unchanged.

- **`dominant` replaces `largest`** — the old name was only correct for a max-heap; `dominant` is neutral across both orderings.

- **`HeapBuilderFactory.createMinHeapBuilder`** — exercises the generalization end-to-end by injecting `MaxHeapCondition.minOrder()` without touching any algorithm code.
